decision.question: Is invoicing from job sheets a problem worth a first validation test?

affected.who: Owners of small landscaping crews (assumed segment)

problem_statement: The founder's own invoicing chore suggests an opportunity, but prevalence, market size and conversion are all unmeasured.

statements.text: The founder runs two landscaping crews and writes invoices from paper job sheets on Sunday evenings.
Other small landscaping operators share the founder's invoicing chore.
Operators would pay a monthly fee to turn job sheets into invoices.
Whether other operators experience this problem is unknown: no interviews exist.
statements.resolution: Run 8 to 10 problem interviews with operators found through the founder's own network, after outreach approval.

statements.text: The number of potential customers is unknown.
statements.resolution: Request approval for public research on registered landscaping businesses; until then no market size is stated.

statements.text: Sign-up conversion for this offer is unknown.
statements.resolution: Measure it with a smoke-test page once outreach and publication are approved.

alternatives.tradeoffs: Slow but direct evidence of prevalence; needs outreach approval.

alternatives.summary: Concierge invoicing for three operators by hand.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Tests willingness to pay with real commitment; costs founder time.

success_measure.metric: Interviewed operators who describe the same chore unprompted

questions.text: May I contact operators from your own network for interviews?

next_action.action: Draft a 10-interview problem script and recruit list; contact nobody until outreach is approved.
